title: Brown Rice with Cheese and/or Cream Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain rice that retains the bran and germ layers. In this version it is served with a cheese and/or cream sauce to which fat (oil or butter) has been added, increasing its energy density and giving a richer mouthfeel.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains more nutrients than white rice, including fiber, B‑vitamins and minerals.
Cheese sauces are often made from processed cheese, cream and spices, creating a smooth, creamy texture.
Adding fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as D and K.
In some Asian cuisines brown rice is combined with dairy products, creating unique hybrid dishes.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs provide sustained energy, beneficial for active individuals and athletes.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B3 and B6 are involved in energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Fat enhances vitamin absorption
items.content: The added fat aids the body’s uptake of fat‑soluble vitamins present in cheese and cream.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Brown rice supplies magnesium, phosphorus and iron, important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The added fat and cheese sauce significantly increase the dish’s calories, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream sauces may contain lactose, making the dish unsuitable for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to cheese or cream.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared cheese sauces often contain salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a side dish with meat, fish or vegetable stews, use as a base for casseroles, or toss into salads. It pairs well with herbs, spices (black pepper, paprika) and a squeeze of lemon.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
